Simulate an outbreak

Source: R/make_outbreak.R
make_outbreak.Rd

Simulates nosocomial outbreaks. Each individual can be infected once, and new cases become infectious from the following day.

Usage

make_outbreak(timeline, imported, w, dates, intervention, mixing = NULL)

Arguments

timeline

A population timeline from make_timeline().

imported

Data frame with id and date (infection date) for imported cases.

w

Probability mass function of the generation time distribution.

dates

Dates over which to simulate transmission.

intervention

Function of present and date returning the matrix E(t) of proportional hazard reductions (0 = none, 1 = complete), as defined in METHODS.md, Interventions. Rows represent sources and columns recipients. present contains the daily population, infection status, infection age, and infectiousness.

mixing

Named list of mixing matrices by population attribute. Rows represent source groups and columns recipient groups. Weights are multiplied across attributes. NULL assumes equal mixing.

Value

A nososim_outbreak containing the population timeline, infection records (id, source, date_infection), simulation dates, and parameters. Imported cases have NA sources.

Examples

dates <- as.Date("2026-01-01") + 0:6
timeline <- make_timeline(10, dates, stay = 7,
attributes = list(
 ward = c(A = 0.5, B = 0.5),
role = c(patient = 0.8, staff = 0.2)
))

imported <- data.frame(id = "ID_1", date = dates[1])

global_ipc <- function(present, date) {
  E_t <- matrix(
    0, nrow(present), nrow(present),
    dimnames = list(present$id, present$id)
  )
  if (date >= dates[4]) E_t[,] <- 0.9
  E_t
}

staff_masking <- function(present, date) {
  E_t <- matrix(
    0, nrow(present), nrow(present),
    dimnames = list(present$id, present$id)
  )
  E_t[present$role == "staff", ] <- 0.9
  E_t
}

A_to_B_IPC <- function(present, date) {
  E_t <- matrix(
    0, nrow(present), nrow(present),
    dimnames = list(present$id, present$id)
  )
  E_t[present$ward == "A", present$ward == "B"] <- 0.9
  E_t
}

make_outbreak(timeline, imported, w = c(0.2, 0.5, 0.3),
  dates, intervention = A_to_B_IPC
)
#> <nososim_outbreak>
#> # A tibble: 1 × 7
#>   individuals simulation_days initial_cases secondary_cases total_cases
#>         <int>           <int>         <int>           <int>       <int>
#> 1          10               7             1               2           3
#> # ℹ 2 more variables: first_case <date>, last_case <date>
